notable_absence.finding: Several parameters (natural, natural_cred, natural_orgid, natural_context, natural_output, use_replica, and the underscore-masking behavior of named parameters) are explicitly gated with 'Couchbase Server X.Y and later' language - exactly the shape the availableSince relation was designed for on server/ pages. Per the batch instructions, availableSince is not asserted here because Capella has no discrete version numbers; this gating language on a Capella page is itself the interesting signal (see cross_product_finding).

cross_product_finding: This Capella page repeatedly gates parameters using literal Couchbase Server version numbers, e.g. 'This parameter is available in clusters running Couchbase Server 8.0 and later' (natural/natural_cred/natural_orgid/natural_context/natural_output), 'Reading from replica is only possible if the cluster uses Couchbase Server 7.6.0 or later' (use_replica), and 'Parameter masking is available in clusters running Couchbase Server 7.6.8 and later' (named parameters). It also links directly into server/ docs via absolute paths, e.g. '/server/8.0/learn/data/durability.html' and '/server/8.0/learn/data/transactions.html'. This strongly suggests the page is generated from largely the same source content as server/'s n1ql-manage/query-settings.md (server/current, server/7.6, server/7.2 all exist) with insufficient adaptation for a versionless Capella audience - a user reading this Capella page has no way to know what 'Couchbase Server 8.0' corresponds to in their Capella cluster.
